$comment: Every cost Sill publishes, and where each one can honestly be taken.
This file holds decisions, never measurements. `what` and `budget` are
copied from a row of docs/budgets.md and verify:source refuses them if
that row stops saying both, so the public page and the internal contract
cannot drift. The readings come from docs/measurements/, which nothing
here and nobody by hand ever writes: they are what a measuring script
concluded, with the build and the machine it concluded it on.
`runs` is where a row can honestly be taken, and it is why the page
has two tables. `anywhere` is counts, ratios, sizes and structural
facts, which mean the same on a borrowed virtual machine as on a desk.
`dedicated` is milliseconds and megabytes of a running launcher, which
need a display, a graphics driver and a machine nobody is using. Showing
the two kinds in one table would say they were the same kind of claim.
Costs whose reading means the same in a development build as in a
release one, so a reading taken on either is a reading.
Everything else is marked provisional on the page until it comes from a
release build, because that is the build the budgets are about and the
two are two orders of magnitude apart in the part of Sill that draws
pixels. These are the exceptions rather than the rule, and they are a
list rather than a default: a new cost is provisional until somebody
argues here that the build cannot change it.
